prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Give Your Desktop Pet a Name", "Personalize your companion before meeting them on your desktop.", "Pet Name", "Continue to Desktop"]
1: ["Select Your Ideal Companion", "Explore pet personalities and traits suited for your daily workflow.", "Playful & Energetic", "Calm & Focused"]
2: ["What Activities Will You Do Together?", "Select daily routines to tailor your pet's future responses while generation completes.", "Work Focus / Casual Breaks", "Save Preferences", "Your pet preferences are being applied."]
3: ["Choose How to Create Your Desktop Pet", "Quick Pick Companion", "Custom AI Pet"]
4: ["Signing in syncs your pets across devices and prevents data reset."]
5: ["Your Companion is Ready on Your Desktop!", "Look at your desktop screen corner. Click on your pet anytime to chat, move, or access settings."]
6: ["Estimated wait time: under 2 minutes"]
7: ["Use well-lit, front-facing photos for optimal custom pet generation results."]
8: ["Quick 3-step setup"]
9: ["We will send a desktop alert as soon as your pet is ready!"]
